content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are a staple item in fast‑food and restaurant menus. They are usually deep‑fried and served with a variety of sauces or seasonings such as barbecue, hot chili, honey‑mustard, garlic aioli, and many others.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are often called "wings" and have become a symbol of American street food.
The most famous wing event is the Buffalo Wing Festival in Buffalo, where the original Buffalo sauce was created.
In the United States more than 1.3 billion servings of chicken wings are consumed each year.
Wings can be prepared not only by deep‑frying but also by baking, grilling, or air‑frying.
A wide range of sauces allows the dish to be adapted to any taste preference—from sweet to extremely spicy.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Wings contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Wings provide iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of sauces
items.content: Some sauces (e.g., garlic or ginger based) add antioxidants that enhance the dish’s overall benefit.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑fried wings are rich in saturated fat and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Spicy sauces
items.content: Hot sauces can irritate the stomach and esophagus in people with sensitive gastrointestinal tracts.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may have an allergic reaction to chicken proteins.

items.title: Salt in sauces
items.content: Many sauces contain a lot of sodium, which may raise blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are typically served hot, with the meat pulled off the bone. They are eaten with the hands, dipped in sauce, and optionally sprinkled with extra seasoning. Common side dishes include fries, onion rings, and fresh vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked fried wings should be stored in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days in an airtight container. They can be reheated in an oven or microwave. Raw frozen wings keep for up to 6 months.
